instruction: Move file1 into dir1, then create symbolic links to dir1/file1 in both dir2 and dir3.

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

result.command: bash -c '[ -f /home/user/dir1/file1 ] && echo "FILE_IN_DIR1:YES" || echo "FILE_IN_DIR1:NO"; [ ! -e /home/user/file1 ] && echo "FILE1_REMOVED:YES" || echo "FILE1_REMOVED:NO"; [ -L /home/user/dir2/file1 ] && echo "SYMLINK_DIR2:YES" || echo "SYMLINK_DIR2:NO"; [ -L /home/user/dir3/file1 ] && echo "SYMLINK_DIR3:YES" || echo "SYMLINK_DIR3:NO"'

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully copied file1 to dir1, dir2, dir3 using cp commands with && chaining, then verified with ls -la. Completed in 9 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use terminal, execute file operations (cp, ls, mv), chain commands with &&, verify results
metadata.task_rationale: Extends copy task to move + symlink creation, testing deeper file operation knowledge while using same setup
metadata.explanation: Task requires moving file1 to dir1 (not copying), then creating symbolic links in dir2 and dir3 pointing to dir1/file1. Evaluator runs bash checks for: (1) file1 exists as regular file in dir1, (2) file1 no longer in home, (3) dir2/file1 is symlink, (4) dir3/file1 is symlink. Partial credit: 0.25 per check.

scoring_breakdown.file_in_dir1: 0.25 - file1 exists as regular file in dir1
scoring_breakdown.file1_removed: 0.25 - file1 no longer exists in home directory

llm_judge_reasons: Getter command correctly checks all 4 aspects: file exists in dir1 (-f), file removed from home (! -e), dir2/file1 is symlink (-L), dir3/file1 is symlink (-L)
Instruction coverage is complete: move operation verified by checking both destination existence and source removal; symlink creation verified in both dir2 and dir3
Partial credit scoring (0.25 per check) is reasonable and well-structured
Minor gap: Symlink target is not verified. The -L test only checks if a symlink exists, not that it points to /home/user/dir1/file1. A symlink pointing to a wrong target would still pass.

The expected rules dict values (true booleans) are never actually used by the metric function, which only parses the result string for YES/NO patterns. This is harmless but indicates a disconnect between expected config and metric logic.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add symlink target verification to the getter command, e.g.: readlink /home/user/dir2/file1 and check it equals /home/user/dir1/file1
Example enhanced check: [ "$(readlink /home/user/dir2/file1)" = "/home/user/dir1/file1" ] && echo SYMLINK_DIR2_TARGET:YES || echo SYMLINK_DIR2_TARGET:NO
